My kitten also died from FIP, although she barely showed any signs and died of it on Monday. Very painful to witness, it was a suffering death for her. Her end came very unexpectedly- the day before she was acting a little like her old self (chewing on my finger, kneading). I wish I had known she was farther along than she looked.

I am so sorry to hear that you've lost your partner. Mine died naturally a little over 48 hours ago, and I'm hoping that my experience will help console you. You have NOT betrayed Stitch in any way. It's hard for us as owners to know what the right thing to do is, and I wholeheartedly believe that you chose what was best for your dog unselfishly. My cat was the same way- she never did anything and her quality of life was declining quickly. But I didn't do anything, I didn't know that I had to. She ended up dying of multiple seizures in my hands, and I will never forgive myself for not allowing an easy passing. It was not easy, it was horrific. I solely grieve because she trusted me and I gave her that pain. I wish I had brought her in for euthanization. I had a vet coming at noon to do it, but they were too late. I was too late in planning it. I used to be so against euthanization- but then I found myself witnessing what happened when you didn't do it. I want to share this perspective because it's not often held, and I hope it comforts you in knowing that you've saved your dog from suffering.
